report.headline: Usage rate projected to climb to a EuroLeague-average share, but the shooting-efficiency number carries no signal

projection.text: Usage rate is projected at 22.1% in the EuroLeague, up from 15.3% in the 2007-08 NBA season, landing close to the 2008-09 EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.6% (sd 4.4%).

risks.text: Source-season usage rate was low at 15.3%, 0.97 standard deviations below the NBA average, the weakest part of the profile.

The true shooting projection of 63.6% comes from a model that performs no better than a simple league-mean baseline (4.7% MAE either way), so despite a much higher z-preservation baseline of 70.9%, this projection should not be treated as informative.

The true shooting slope of 0.534 shows only about half of a player's shooting-efficiency standing typically carries over on this transition, far less than the near-full carryover seen for usage (0.982).

The estimate rests on 115 historical NBA->EL transitions in which movers were, on average, slightly below their own league's mean (-0.31 sd) rather than clearly above it, an atypical selection pattern to generalize from.

strengths.text: True shooting efficiency sat 1.93 standard deviations above the NBA average (64.7%) in the source season, the standout number in the profile.
Projected usage of 22.1% is within a point and a half of the EuroLeague average, suggesting a central rather than marginal role in the new league.
The fitted usage slope for this transition is 0.982, close to full carryover, meaning players who make this move tend to retain almost all of their prior usage standing.
The source season was a full workload of 2,274 minutes across 76 games, indicating an established role rather than a small sample.

uncertainty.text: The 80% interval for usage runs 17.6%-26.5%, a span of roughly two league standard deviations (sd 4.4%), and the 95% interval widens further to 15.3%-28.8%; the model does modestly beat a league-mean baseline here (3.3% MAE vs 4.3%), so it can rank this player within a broad band but not pin down a precise figure.
